newsitem.title: USA: NYC says World Series, Marathon produce $161 mln.
newsitem.headline: NYC says World Series, Marathon produce $161 mln.

text.p: New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani on Tuesday said that having the Yankees play and win the six-game World Series, plus holding the New York City Marathon, was worth over $161 million to the city.

Of all these events, the 27th annual marathon on November 3, which attracted nearly 30,000 runners, was the most valuable single event for the city, spurring the biggest rise in spending, which was estimated at $97.8 million.

The mayor released the report late Tuesday. Alan Hevesi, the city comptroller, scheduled a news conference on Wednesday at 1030 EST to release a report on how much professional and amateur teams and sports associations contribute to the local economy. A spokesman for Hevesi, who is seen as a potential Democratic challenger to the Republican mayor, declined to disclose details about his report.

The Giuliani Administration said its data on the marathon was based on how much the New York Road Runners Club spent, as well as the expenses run up by runners, guests, New York City and spectators, for food and transportation. The report also estimated how much these people spent in stores and on other amusements and recreation, plus the 'ripple effect' of such spending.

Each of the three home games in the World Series produced around $10.9 million, the Giuliani Administration said, adding the series generated $32.6 million, counting ticket, concession and merchandise sales, parking fees, and tourist spending.
And the ticker tape parade for the Yankees was another big-ticket item, producing $30.8 million, Giuliani said, saying 3.5 million people went to the parade.

"With the World Series Championship and the incredible ticker tape parade that followed, along with the 27th Annual New York City Marathon, New York City proves once again it is the sporting capital of the world," Giuliani said, in prepared comments.
